SL-000055.transcript:
Member (Lucas Patel): The pharmacy said my new prescription needs another form before you'll cover it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Lucas Patel, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Lucas Patel): I uploaded the prescription through the app already.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Lucas Patel): Yes, that's right.
Member (Lucas Patel): My doctor charges 45 dollars to fill in forms.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which medication or service is the request about?
Member (Lucas Patel): A new medication my specialist started me on last week.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the pharmacy give you the name of the form they need?
Member (Lucas Patel): They said 'prior authorization' and gave me a number to call. That's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Is your doctor's office aware a form is needed?
Member (Lucas Patel): I told them, and they said they'd need the form itself from Sun Life.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've checked the information request and the documents already on file.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): For this medication the plan needs a prior authorization from your doctor, not just the prescription.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I'm checking whether anything from your doctor's office is already on file.
Member (Lucas Patel): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The prior authorization form is on file from last week. It just wasn't linked to the drug claim. I've linked it, and the pharmacy can resubmit today.
Member (Lucas Patel): So I can pick it up today?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Yes. The authorization is linked to the claim now, so the pharmacy can resubmit and it should go through.
Member (Lucas Patel): Will I have to do this every time?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): No. It's approved for twelve months, so refills go through automatically.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): So you're all set: the authorization is on file for twelve months and the pharmacy can process it today.
Member (Lucas Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-000102.transcript:
Member (Leila Wilson): My Canadian Dental Care Plan crown request was denied and even the supervisor couldn't tell me why.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Leila Wilson, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.
Member (Leila Wilson): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Leila Wilson): The member ID is on the welcome letter.
Member (Leila Wilson): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Leila Wilson): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Is this the first request or a resubmission?
Member (Leila Wilson): The second. The first was denied in July.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Are you in any pain right now?
Member (Leila Wilson): Some. It's manageable, but I can't chew on that side.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): The assessment is done against the plan's criteria for crowns, which are set by Health Canada.
Member (Leila Wilson): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): The first request was missing the radiograph date. The second one is complete and has been assessed, and it's approved. Your dentist will get the confirmation today.
Member (Leila Wilson): So the crown is covered now?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Yes. It's approved at your plan's coverage level, and your dentist will get the confirmation today.
Member (Leila Wilson): Do I pay anything?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): That depends on your co-payment level. Your dentist will see it on the confirmation.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): To recap: the crown is approved, and your dentist will get the confirmation today with your co-payment.
Member (Leila Wilson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-000195.transcript:
Member (Mei Cote): My Canadian Dental Care Plan crown request was denied and even the supervisor couldn't tell me why.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Mei Cote, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mei Cote): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Mei Cote): Yes, that's right.
Member (Mei Cote): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Mei Cote): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Is this the first request or a resubmission?
Member (Mei Cote): The second. The first was denied in July.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Did the letter mention any documents that were missing?
Member (Mei Cote): No, just that it doesn't meet the criteria.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The assessment is done against the plan's criteria for crowns, which are set by Health Canada.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Mei Cote): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Mei Cote): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Mei Cote): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Mei Cote): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-000196.transcript:
Member (Fatima Wilson): I'm waiting on a decision on my disability claim and nobody has called me.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Fatima Wilson, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Fatima Wilson): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Fatima Wilson): Yes, that's right.
Member (Fatima Wilson): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): When did you go off work?
Member (Fatima Wilson): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Fatima Wilson): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Have you been contacted by a case manager yet?
Member (Fatima Wilson): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Is there a good number and time to reach you?
Member (Fatima Wilson): My mobile, any time before three. I have appointments in the afternoons.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Fatima Wilson): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your claim was approved yesterday. The first payment goes out Friday, and your case manager will call you this week to talk about your return-to-work plan.
Member (Fatima Wilson): So when does the first payment come?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): It's scheduled for Friday, and it includes the weeks since your waiting period ended.
Member (Fatima Wilson): Who do I contact if something changes?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your case manager is Denise. I've sent you her direct line by secure message.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: your claim is approved, the first payment is Friday, and Denise will call this week about your return-to-work plan.
Member (Fatima Wilson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Gurpreet Kim): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Gurpreet Kim): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Gurpreet Kim): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Gurpreet Kim): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Gurpreet Kim): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Gurpreet Kim): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Gurpreet Kim): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Gurpreet Kim): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Gurpreet Kim): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Member (Gurpreet Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Fatima Roy): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Hi Fatima Roy, Aisha Rahman here — let me pull that up.
Member (Fatima Roy): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Fatima Roy): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Fatima Roy): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Fatima Roy): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Fatima Roy): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Fatima Roy): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Fatima Roy): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Fatima Roy): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Fatima Roy): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Fatima Roy): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Fatima Roy): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Fatima Roy): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

SL-000642.transcript:
Member (Chantal Wilson): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Chantal Wilson, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Chantal Wilson): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Chantal Wilson): Yes, that's right.
Member (Chantal Wilson): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Chantal Wilson): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Chantal Wilson): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Chantal Wilson): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Chantal Wilson): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Chantal Wilson): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Chantal Wilson): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Chantal Wilson): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Chantal Wilson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Hannah Campbell): My Canadian Dental Care Plan crown request was denied and even the supervisor couldn't tell me why.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Hannah Campbell, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Hannah Campbell): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): That depends on your co-payment level. Your dentist will see it on the confirmation.

Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Gurpreet Patel, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.
Member (Gurpreet Patel): It went from about 250 to 750 dollars a month.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Gurpreet Patel): Yes, that's right.
Member (Gurpreet Patel): I called two weeks before the renewal date to cancel.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Which policy is this about?
Member (Gurpreet Patel): My term life policy. It renewed this month.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Did you get a confirmation of the cancellation?
Member (Gurpreet Patel): No, I was told it would be processed.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): How much was taken, and on what date?
Member (Gurpreet Patel): 750 dollars on the 1st.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): If the cost came down, would you want to keep some coverage?

Agent (Marc Tremblay): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I can see your call from the 17th and the renewal payment taken on the 1st.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The renewal rate is higher because the policy moved into a new age band on renewal.
Member (Gurpreet Patel): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The cancellation was processed after the renewal draft had already gone through. I've requested the refund, and it'll be back in your account within seven business days.
Member (Gurpreet Patel): So I get the full 750 back?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Yes, the full amount. The refund request is approved and goes back to the same account.
Member (Gurpreet Patel): Will I get something in writing?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Yes, a cancellation confirmation by mail within ten days.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): To recap: the policy is cancelled, the 750 dollars is on its way back, and a written confirmation will follow.
Member (Gurpreet Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-000843.transcript:
Member (Emma Chen): I asked to transfer my pension from my old employer's plan to my bank and it still hasn't moved.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Emma Chen, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.
Member (Emma Chen): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Emma Chen): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Emma Chen): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Which plan is the transfer from?
Member (Emma Chen): My old employer's pension plan. I left the company in May.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Where is the money going?
Member (Emma Chen): To an RRSP at my bank. They say they're waiting on Sun Life.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Did the bank send you a transfer form to sign as well?
Member (Emma Chen): I think so. They handled their side.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Have you received any statement showing the transfer as pending?
Member (Emma Chen): Only the annual statement, which still shows the balance with you.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Let me take a look. I've traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Your request came in on June 14. The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer authorization from the receiving institution, which is standard for locked-in pension money.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Emma Chen): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): The transfer was held because the receiving institution's form wasn't signed. It came in this morning, so I've released it, and the funds will move within five business days.
Member (Emma Chen): So it's finally moving?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Yes. The form arrived this morning, and I've released the transfer.
Member (Emma Chen): How long until my bank has it?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Usually five business days, and you'll get a confirmation letter from us.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): So the transfer is released and should reach your bank within five business days.
Member (Emma Chen): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Mei Cote): The chat assistant told me to call. I've been on hold for over an hour.

Member (Mei Cote): And if it locks again?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Use the 'forgot password' link only once, then wait 30 minutes. I've added a note in case you need to call.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Member (Mei Cote): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Arjun Singh): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Hi Arjun Singh, Chloe Gagnon here — let me pull that up.
Member (Arjun Singh): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Arjun Singh): The member ID is on the welcome letter.
Member (Arjun Singh): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Arjun Singh): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Did the letter mention any documents that were missing?
Member (Arjun Singh): No, just that it doesn't meet the criteria.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Arjun Singh): They said they called and got the same answer as me.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Are you in any pain right now?
Member (Arjun Singh): Some. It's manageable, but I can't chew on that side.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): The assessment is done against the plan's criteria for crowns, which are set by Health Canada.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Arjun Singh): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Arjun Singh): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Arjun Singh): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Arjun Singh): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Owen Chen): I've been off work for six weeks and still haven't had a decision on my short-term disability claim.

Agent (Daniel Okafor): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.

Member (Owen Chen): So when does the first payment come?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): It's scheduled for Friday, and it includes the weeks since your waiting period ended.
Member (Owen Chen): Who do I contact if something changes?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Your case manager is Denise. I've sent you her direct line by secure message.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): To recap: your claim is approved, the first payment is Friday, and Denise will call this week about your return-to-work plan.
Member (Owen Chen): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Emma Lavoie): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Emma Lavoie, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Emma Lavoie): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Emma Lavoie): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Emma Lavoie): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Emma Lavoie): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Emma Lavoie): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Emma Lavoie): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Emma Lavoie): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Emma Lavoie): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Emma Lavoie): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Emma Lavoie): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Emma Lavoie): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.

Member (Owen Patel): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Owen Patel): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Owen Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Hannah Cote): My son needs braces and I want to know what my plan pays before we commit.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Hannah Cote, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.
Member (Hannah Cote): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Good question to ask before you commit. Let me look.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Hannah Cote): Yes, that's right.
Member (Hannah Cote): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): How old is he?
Member (Hannah Cote): Fourteen.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?

Agent (Jasmine Wong): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?

Agent (Jasmine Wong): Is the orthodontist here in Canada?

Agent (Jasmine Wong): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.

Agent (Jasmine Wong): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Hannah Cote): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Hannah Cote): Great, that helps.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.
Member (Hannah Cote): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
